newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX index ends thin bourse trade weaker.
newsitem.headline: German DAX index ends thin bourse trade weaker.

text.p: German blue chip shares closed thin-volume floor trading weaker on Tuesday, but dealers said the market had not changed course and was just taking time to consolidate after climbing to new highs in the last few weeks.
The 30-share DAX index of blue-chip stocks closed down 11.47 points or 0.42 percent at 2,691.17.
"We can slide a little bit or move sideways over the next few days and then take another run up beyond 2,700," said one trader.
Meanwhile the MDAX index of 70 medium-sized companies moved in the opposite direction and reached a new record mid-session of 3001.81, before closing at 2,998.32, up 13.24 points, or 0.4 percent.

MDAX constituent sportswear manufacturer adidas led the way to jump three marks in bourse trade to a year-high of 145 marks on the back of news that it would be an official sponsor for the 1998 soccer World Cup.
The stock closed bourse trade at 143.40 marks.

Metals and trading company Metallgesellschaft was the day's best performer on the DAX, climbing over four percent to reach 28.58 marks, after the firm said profits for the 1995/1996 financial year would definitely top the previous year.
The group's management board chairman said the firm had done "extraordinarily well" in a difficult area.

Airline Deutsche Lufthansa also moved against the trend, hiitng a session high of 224 marks after it said a co-operative alliance with Scandinavian airline SAS would improve its net earnings by 100 million marks in 1997.
Later Lufthansa shares came off somewhat and ended bourse trade at 221.70, up 1.20 marks.
